tips.title: Photo tips
tips.intro: A good photo gives a better cutout, a better listing and better studio shots.

clutter.bad: A busy background with other things in the frame
clutter.good: One product on a plain cloth, table or wall

distance.bad: The product small in the middle of a wide shot
distance.good: Step closer so the product fills most of the frame

light.bad: A dark room, or a flash that leaves hard shadows
light.good: Daylight from a window, beside you rather than behind the product

keys.q: Where do I find my WooCommerce keys?
keys.a: In your WordPress admin, open WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API, then Add key. Choose Read/Write, generate it, and paste the consumer key and secret into Connections. ListSnap encrypts them and never shows them again.

draft.q: Why is my product a draft?
draft.a: ListSnap never publishes for you. Every product goes to your store as a draft, so you can check it there and publish when you're ready.

edit.q: Can I edit after saving to the store?
edit.a: Yes. Change anything on Review and press Update store draft: the same draft is updated, never copied.

labels.q: What do the AI labels mean?
labels.a: AI background: your real product photo on a background made by AI. AI scene: the whole picture is an AI edit around your product, so check it still looks like what you sell.

limits.a: Each shop can start {listings, number} listings and make {photos, number} AI photos and {reels, number} reels a day. They start again at 6:00 AM Bangladesh time. Usage shows where you are.

missed.q: The AI didn't find my product. What now?
missed.a: Press Try again, or take the photo again closer, on a plain background and in good light. Several products in one photo? You can choose which to keep and how to group them.

data.a: Your photos are kept for your shop and sent to Meta's models (Muse Spark, SAM 3.1 and Muse Image) only to make your listings. Store keys are encrypted. Nothing is sold or shared with anyone else.

export.title: Sell on Facebook Marketplace and other sites
export.intro: Export makes files you can post anywhere, even without a connected store.

steps.kit: On Review, press Export and choose Listing kit. On a phone, Share photos sends them straight to the Facebook app and copies the text.
steps.post: In Marketplace, create a listing, add the photos, and copy each block of listing-en.txt or listing-bn.txt into the matching field.
steps.many: To export many at once, tick them on Listings and press Export: you get a kit for each, plus CSV files for a Facebook catalog, WooCommerce and Shopify.
steps.shopify: When you import the Shopify file, untick "Publish new products to all sales channels" in Shopify's Import window. The products arrive as drafts either way.
steps.website: The Facebook catalog file needs your shop's website or Facebook Page, set in Settings.

export.note: Facebook says Marketplace is for personal items. A business should sell through a Facebook Shop or ads; the catalog file works for both.

readme.title: ListSnap export: what goes where
readme.kits: Each folder is one listing: its photos, and its text in listing-en.txt and listing-bn.txt. For Facebook Marketplace, Daraz or any other site, add the photos and copy each block of text into the matching field.
readme.facebook: catalog-facebook.csv: in Meta Commerce Manager, open your catalog, then Data sources → Data feed → Upload once, and choose this file.
readme.facebookMissing: There is no Facebook catalog file: add your shop's website or Facebook Page in ListSnap's Settings, then export again.
readme.woocommerce: products-woocommerce.csv: in WordPress, open Products → Import. The products arrive as drafts.
readme.shopify: products-shopify.csv: in Shopify admin, open Products → Import. Untick "Publish new products to all sales channels" before you import. The products arrive as drafts.
readme.links: The photo links in the CSV files work for 30 days. Import before then, or export again.
